name: M33SSS J013337.47+303138.8
description: A Cepheid in the Triangulum Galaxy that pulsates every 57.7 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 57.68 d in Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118, table 9 (log P 1.761); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 57.68 d in Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118, table 9 (log P 1.761); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M33, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2012AJ....144....4M; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M33 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 858,887 pc (src/objects/m33/source/recipe.json: centre 859,014 pc from the Local Volume Database v1.1.1 (Pace 2025), inclination 54 deg, line of nodes 22.5 deg). The galaxy's Cepheid distance, Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118, abstract: modulus 24.622 +/- 0.03 mag, 840 kpc; it places the galaxy, not a star within it

text.card: A Cepheid in the Triangulum Galaxy, 840 kiloparsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 57.7 days.
text.introduction: The Hubble Space Telescope measured its brightness in three colours; its pulsation takes 57.7 days. Its galaxy's distance, 840 kiloparsecs, was measured from Cepheids like it.
text.locator: table 9, ID 01333747+3031388: logP; Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118: mu

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M33 is not measured
